claims.promise: A flight entry is written to the device as it is typed, survives a crash or an app that is closed mid-entry, and is never silently unsaved, so a logbook that a licence depends on cannot lose a flight.

evidence.finding: Safelog, 3.0 stars over 10K+ installs, draws a 1-star review reading "it constantly crashes, 100% of the time while I'm in the middle of entering my flight times", and crash is 4 of the 10 critical reviews read on this shelf.

claims.deferredReason: Persistence on every edit and the crash-recovery path are unbuilt; the promise is resolved only when a test fails against a batch-write-on-exit implementation.

claims.promise: The logbook is the pilot's own file: no account, no mandatory cloud sync that can drop entries, and a backup that restores exactly what was written.

evidence.finding: Garmin Pilot, 2.8 stars over 500K+ installs, draws a 2-star review reading "Doesn't save anything anymore. I've used this app on Android for the past year as a student pilot", and data-loss appears in 3 of the 10 critical reviews read.

claims.deferredReason: Local storage and the restore path do not exist yet; the promise is resolved when a backup taken from one install restores into a clean one in a test.

claims.promise: Every column and running total a licence needs is editable and correct, and a summary prints for an examiner or an insurer, so the logbook is evidence rather than a personal notebook.

evidence.finding: missing-feature is 3 of the 10 critical reviews read (30 percent) and confusing-ui 2 of 10, while 26 of 30 visible titles on the pilot logbook query do this job and 7 of the 15 rated ones sit below 4.2 stars.

claims.deferredReason: The column set and the totals rule are unbuilt; the promise is resolved when a fixture asserts each total against a hand-computed reference logbook.

claims.promise: It is bought once with no subscription and no advertising, so a pilot who flies twice a month is not paying a monthly fee to keep his own record readable.

evidence.finding: docs/monetization-strategy.md section 3.1 records the single unlock as the archetype for this class of local tool, and every top app measured on the shelf is free with in-app purchases rather than a one-time price.

claims.deferredReason: Billing is not wired up and the unlock sheet does not exist; it is resolved when the purchase is the only paywall in the shipped app.

claims.promise: The logbook works with no signal, in a cockpit or on a ramp, because nothing in the entry path waits on a network call.

evidence.finding: The weakest measured apps on this shelf are the ones that route the record through a sync, and the plan enables no network capability and no server.

claims.deferredReason: The offline guarantee is unbuilt; it is resolved when a test proves the entry path makes no network call.
